hints: Look carefully at the positions of the H atoms and the $\text{-COOH}$ groups around the $\text{C=C}$ bond in X and Y.
In X both $\text{-COOH}$ groups are on the same side of the double bond, so identify whether this is cis or trans.
Think about what happens to cis-trans isomerism when the $\text{C=C}$ bond and the acid groups are fully reduced to single bonds.
walkthrough:
**Assign cis and trans in X and Y**

Look at the $\text{C=C}$ bond. Cis means the same two groups are on the same side, trans means they are on opposite sides.

In X, the two $\text{H}$ atoms are both below the $\text{C=C}$ and the two $\text{-COOH}$ groups are both above. In Y, they are on opposite sides. So X is cis (maleic acid) and Y is trans (fumaric acid).

**Work out what reduction does**

Both acids have formula $\text{HOOCCH=CHCOOH}$, which is $\text{C}_4\text{H}_4\text{O}_4$.

Full reduction converts $\text{C=C}$ to $\text{C-C}$ and each $\text{-COOH}$ to $\text{-CH}_2\text{OH}$:
$$\text{HOOCCH=CHCOOH} \rightarrow \text{HOCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$$

**Check the product formula and identity**

The product is butane-1,4-diol, $\text{C}_4\text{H}_{10}\text{O}_2$.

Its empirical formula is $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{O}$, matching P and Q. Because the $\text{C=C}$ is gone, there is no more cis-trans isomerism, so P from X and Q from Y must be the identical molecule.

options.A: Correct. X has identical groups on the same side so it is the cis isomer. Reduction removes the double bond, so the stereochemical difference is lost and P and Q are both butane-1,4-diol, identical.
options.B: Half right but half wrong. X is indeed cis, but P and Q cannot be isomers of each other because full reduction gives a saturated diol with free rotation and no E/Z isomerism.
options.C: Incorrect assignment. X is not trans. Trans has the $\text{-COOH}$ groups on opposite sides, which is structure Y. The second part about P and Q being identical is true, but the first part fails.
options.D: Incorrect on both parts. X is cis, not trans, and reduction destroys the $\text{C=C}$ stereocentre so P and Q are identical, not isomers.
